Eventually, her mother learns the truth about Nell's innocence regarding the wine and permits their friendship to resume. Lucy attends the Brierley Debating Club concert alongside Nell, sleeping over at the Pembroke home where they accidentally jump onto Aunt Lavinia in the spare room. unit: John Ashdown, a widowed Presbyterian minister with four children, receives the call to pastor the church in Brierley (Glen St. Agnes) and moves into the manse with his children—Tobias, Grace, Ida, and Rupert—and elderly Aunt Martha. His scholarly, highly spiritual preaching quickly earns the deep respect of his congregation. Due to his profound absent-mindedness and absorption in study, his children run wild and get into various public scrapes, causing village gossip, though his affection for them is deep. Struggling with guilt over his perceived failings as a father after several incidents, he considers remarriage but refuses to marry without true affection. He grows close to Clementine Ainslie, finding a deep soul-connection with her. After her initial hesitation due to an old vow made to her sister Harriet, the couple overcomes the obstacle and marries.

Having resigned his charge in the previous February, he departed surrounded by the regrets of his congregation, the majority of whom possessed the affection arising from prolonged contact for their good old minister, notwithstanding his deficiencies as a speaker. Later, overhearing her father's deep sorrow and believing he needs a companion, Ida bravely walks to the house on the hill to personally ask Clementine Ainslie to marry him.
